summary: Multi-agent software-engineering studies show promising role specialization on benchmark and prototype tasks. They do not yet demonstrate that organization-like agent workforces reliably outperform simpler agents under real maintenance costs and shared failure modes.

items.text: ChatDev (ACL 2024) evaluates a role-playing multi-agent software company on generated software tasks and reports improvements over several baselines; synthetic tasks and framework-specific choices limit production claims.

MetaGPT (ICLR 2024) encodes standardized operating procedures into role-specialized agents and evaluates collaborative software generation; results support structured roles but not arbitrary workforce scaling.
A 2025 systematic literature review in ACM TOSEM synthesizes LLM-based multi-agent systems for software engineering and identifies evaluation, coordination and reproducibility gaps.
AutoGen (2023 preprint) presents a programmable multi-agent conversation framework and case studies; it is foundational system evidence, not an independent causal productivity trial.
